function: p. 5-6: learned joint design of BS communication and sensing beamforming and IOS reflecting/refracting phase shifts and amplitudes, maximizing sum-rate and sensing SNR under outdated, imperfect CSI.
system: p. 11-12: ISAC, BS with N=10 antennas, six single-antenna UEs and one target, IOS (simultaneous reflecting and refracting, STAR-RIS type) with M=30 elements; carrier frequency not stated.
method: p. 7-10: hybrid deep reinforcement learning (D3PG with D2QN, GRU networks) plus Reptile meta-learning over objective-preference weights, then fine-tuning; online training in simulation.
data_channel: p. 4, 10: simulated Rician channels with Gauss-Markov time correlation (rho=0.85) and distance path loss; the agent trains by interacting with the simulator, no dataset.
test_conditions: p. 12-14: meta-training on 30 tasks with random preference weights and positions; testing after adaptation or zero-shot on new weights, positions and NLoS; weight 0.2-0.8, IOS elements 10-40.
baselines: p. 12: AS2 (alternating optimization, SCA, SDR), DoubleIRS DRL [36], DDPG-DQN, MHDRL without meta-learning, and zero-shot meta-MHDRL-z.
metrics: p. 12-13: short-term average sum-rate and sensing SNR over 20 runs; time slots to converge.
complexity: p. 11: forward and back-propagation complexity O(Ne N (N+U) X^2) for MHDRL and O((KL+1) Ne N (N+U) X^2) for meta-MHDRL.
q1_support: p. 4: "The Rician channel model [32] is employed for all channels." is a custom simulator; p. 10: "the agent interacts with a simulation environment built using mathematical models, rather than relying on prior training data". No 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "the positions of the target and UEs as well the NLoS are reconfigured" at meta-adaptation; p. 10: "the agent fine-turns the trained metaparameters using few experiences from the new task"; p. 13: "enabling fairly good performance even when the adaptation environment differs from the training environments".
q3_support: p. 12: "AS2: This scheme combines alternating optimization, successive convex approximation, and semidefinite relaxation methods" is the non-learned baseline; p. 12: "The DRL-based BS beamforming and IRS configuration in [36] is utilized" and "DDPG-DQN: In this scheme, the deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm [33]" are learned; compared on sum-rate and sensing SNR (p. 13).
q4_support: p. 11: "the total computational complexity of meta-MHDRL for both forward-propagation and back-propagation is O((KL + 1)Ne N (N + U )X 2 )".
q5_support: p. 11: "based on Python 3.6 simulation platform [31], where the keras library builds all ANN models"; no code or data link or DOI anywhere, and p. 10 shows training on a simulator, not a public channel dataset.
notes: Area 5: learned beamforming and STAR-RIS configuration in an ISAC system, and the more specific ISAC area wins over area 3. IOS is treated as STARS (p. 1, footnote 1). q2 rests on meta-adaptation and zero-shot tests on new preference weights, positions and NLoS (weights 0.2 and 0.4 lie outside the mainly 0.6-0.8 meta-training range, p. 14); the IOS-element sweep is not counted because p. 11 says the agent retrains when the number of elements changes.
